title: Add deterministic ANSI 256-color rendering
description:
## Source

Parent/source bead: `gs-y9o`.

## What to build

Complete color rendering for the Enhanced status view using deterministic ANSI 256-color styling and Color mode behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Additions render green and deletions render red.
- [ ] Staged section and Staged entries render green.
- [ ] Tracked section and Tracked entries render ANSI 256-color orange.
- [ ] Untracked section and Untracked entries render ANSI 256-color muted gray.
- [ ] `--color=never` emits plain output.
- [ ] `--color=always` emits deterministic ANSI output.
- [ ] `--color=auto` emits color only when stdout is a TTY.
- [ ] Rendered output snapshots cover plain and forced-color output.

## Classification

- Slice type: AFK
- Beads type: task
- Priority: 2
- User stories covered: 7, 8, 9, 10, 25

## Blocked by

- `gs-y9o.2` — slice 2 must complete first.
- `gs-y9o.3` — slice 3 must complete first.
- `gs-y9o.4` — slice 4 must complete first.

## Notes for future agents

Use Deterministic ANSI 256-color styling, not truecolor, basic-ANSI-only yellow fallback, or custom theming. Color is rendering behavior; tests should assert user-visible output rather than internal styling structs.
close_reason: Delivered behavior with tests: implemented complete gs Enhanced status view slice; cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.

title: Add unknown stats and submodule path-level handling
description:
## Source

Parent/source bead: `gs-y9o`.

## What to build

Render binary, non-line-oriented, and parent-visible submodule changes with Unknown stats while keeping submodule internals out of repository inspection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Binary or non-line-oriented changed files render Unknown stats as `+?/-?`.
- [ ] Untracked binary files render `+?/-?`.
- [ ] Submodules are reported only as Submodule path-level change when visible in the parent repository.
- [ ] `gs` does not inspect submodule internals.
- [ ] Tests cover binary/unknown stats and parent-level submodule behavior.

## Classification

- Slice type: AFK
- Beads type: task
- Priority: 2
- User stories covered: 12, 22, 24, 25

## Blocked by

- `gs-y9o.4` — slice 4 must complete first.

## Notes for future agents

Unknown stats must render exactly `+?/-?`; do not render `binary` or `+0/-0`. This slice should not add recursive submodule status or inspect nested worktrees.
close_reason: Delivered behavior with tests: implemented complete gs Enhanced status view slice; cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.

- [ ] Renames sort by destination path.
- [ ] Rename stats render as Known text stats when available, otherwise Unknown stats.

title: Split partially staged files across sections
description:

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Partially staged file renders once in `Staged` and once in `Tracked`.
- [ ] Each rendered Entry has separate staged or unstaged Entry stats.
- [ ] Section count counts rendered entries, not unique paths.
- [ ] Tests cover a partially staged text file with different staged and unstaged stats.

## Classification

- Slice type: AFK
- Beads type: task
- Priority: 2
- User stories covered: 13, 24, 25

## Blocked by

- `gs-y9o.4` — slice 4 must complete first.

## Notes for future agents

Do not combine staged and unstaged stats. This slice protects the meaning of Staged section and Tracked section. Future agents should assert output, not internal libgit2 status flags.

title: PRD: Enhanced Git Status CLI
description:
## Problem Statement

Standard `git status` does not provide a compact, colorized, line-change-aware view of repository changes. The user wants a frequent-use CLI that shows staged, tracked, and untracked changes with per-file addition/deletion counts, clear grouping, useful branch context, and predictable output.

## Solution

Build a Rust CLI named `gs` that prints an enhanced, read-only Git status view for the current repository. It groups changes by section, shows status symbols and line stats per entry, uses deterministic terminal colors, includes compact branch/upstream context, and handles common Git edge cases such as partially staged files, renames, binary files, ignored files, detached HEAD, and clean repositories.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want to run `gs` in a Git repository, so that I can see a more informative status view than standard `git status`.
2. As a developer, I want changes grouped into `Staged`, `Tracked`, and `Untracked`, so that I can immediately understand what is commit-ready, modified but unstaged, or new.
3. As a developer, I want empty sections hidden, so that the output stays compact.
4. As a developer, I want section headers to include entry counts, so that I can quickly scan change volume.
5. As a developer, I want each entry to show a status symbol, filepath, and changed-line stats, so that I can assess change type and size at a glance.
6. As a developer, I want changed-line stats to show additions and deletions, so that I can quickly estimate diff size.
7. As a developer, I want additions shown in green and deletions shown in red, so that change direction is visually obvious.
8. As a developer, I want `Staged` entries styled green, `Tracked` entries styled orange, and `Untracked` entries styled muted gray, so that sections are visually distinct.
9. As a developer, I want deterministic ANSI 256-color output, so that colors are stable across supported terminals.
10. As a developer, I want `--color=auto|always|never`, so that I can control color behavior for terminals, demos, scripts, and tests.
11. As a developer, I want untracked text files shown as all additions, so that new files still have meaningful line stats.
12. As a developer, I want binary or unknown-stat files shown as `+?/-?`, so that changed binary files are visible without misleading counts.
13. As a developer, I want partially staged files to appear separately in staged and tracked sections, so that staged and unstaged diffs are not conflated.
14. As a developer, I want renamed files displayed as old path to new path, so that rename context is preserved.
15. As a developer, I want entries sorted alphabetically by display path, so that files are easy to find.
16. As a developer, I want paths displayed relative to the repository root, so that output is stable regardless of where I run the command.
17. As a developer, I want compact Git-letter symbols, so that output remains familiar and scannable.
18. As a developer, I want a compact branch header with upstream ahead/behind counts, so that I know branch sync state without running another command.
19. As a developer, I want detached HEAD shown clearly, so that repository state is not ambiguous.
20. As a developer, I want a clean repository to show branch context plus a clean message, so that successful no-change output is explicit.
21. As a developer, I want ignored files excluded, so that build artifacts and intentional noise do not clutter status.
22. As a developer, I want submodule internals excluded, so that `gs` reports only parent-repository path-level changes.
23. As a developer, I want `gs` to fail clearly outside a Git repo, so that I understand why no status was shown.
24. As a maintainer, I want the core behavior tested against real temporary Git repositories, so that Git status edge cases remain correct.
25. As a maintainer, I want rendering tested separately, so that layout, color behavior, alignment, and clean output remain stable.
26. As a maintainer, I want the agreed behavior documented, so that future implementation and changes have a durable contract.

## Implementation Decisions

- Build a Rust CLI named `gs`.
- `gs` is read-only: no staging, unstaging, discard, commit, or interactive actions.
- Use a Rust Git library, likely libgit2 bindings, instead of shelling out to the installed Git binary.
- Use a library-plus-thin-binary architecture:
  - Repository inspector
  - Change model/classifier
  - Diff/stat calculator
  - Renderer
  - Thin CLI shell
- Repository inspection opens the current Git repository and discovers parent repositories as expected.
- The repository inspector gathers:
  - branch name
  - detached HEAD state
  - upstream ahead/behind counts
  - staged changes
  - unstaged tracked changes
  - untracked files
  - ignore-rule-aware status
  - parent-repository submodule path-level changes only
- The change model has three visible sections:
  - `Staged`
  - `Tracked`
  - `Untracked`
- Empty sections are hidden.
- Section headers include entry counts.
- Entries use Git-letter symbols:
  - `M` modified
  - `A` added
  - `D` deleted
  - `R` renamed
  - `?` untracked
- Entry lines use:
  - two-space indentation
  - status symbol
  - repository-root-relative display path
  - padding
  - aligned stats column
- Entry stats use `+N/-N` for known text changes.
- Untracked text files are treated as all additions and shown as `+N/-0`.
- Binary or unknown-stat files are shown as `+?/-?`.
- Partially staged files appear in both `Staged` and `Tracked`, with separate staged and unstaged stats.
- Renames display as old path to new path and sort by destination path.
- Entries sort alphabetically by display path.
- Branch header uses compact format:
  - branch name
  - nonzero upstream ahead count
  - nonzero upstream behind count
  - omit missing or zero counts
- Detached HEAD displays as detached plus short commit identifier.
- Clean repositories print branch context followed by `✓ working tree clean`.
- Outside a Git repository, `gs` prints `gs: not a git repository` to stderr and exits with code `1`.
- `gs` supports `--color=auto|always|never`, defaulting to `auto`.
- Color behavior:
  - additions: green
  - deletions: red
  - staged section/entries: green
  - tracked section/entries: ANSI 256-color orange
  - untracked section/entries: ANSI 256-color muted gray
- Ignored files are not shown.
- Submodule internals are not inspected.
- A project README should capture usage, output behavior, edge cases, and testing expectations.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should verify external behavior, not implementation details.
- Repository behavior should be tested with temporary Git repositories.
- Rendering behavior should be testable independently from repository inspection.
- The repository inspector/change model should be covered for:
  - clean repository
  - staged changes
  - unstaged tracked changes
  - untracked text files
  - partially staged files
  - renamed files
  - binary or unknown-stat files
  - ignored files excluded
  - branch header with upstream
  - branch header without upstream
  - detached HEAD
  - outside-repository error
  - submodule path-level behavior without inspecting internals
- The renderer should be covered for:
  - plain output with color disabled
  - forced-color output
  - aligned stats columns
  - section counts
  - hidden empty sections
  - clean repository output
  - `+?/-?` display for unknown stats
- Good tests should assert stable user-visible output and observable exit/error behavior.
- Snapshot-style assertions are appropriate for rendered output because layout and color are part of the product contract.
- No prior project test patterns exist because the repository currently has no Rust project initialized.

## Out of Scope

- Interactive staging, unstaging, discarding, committing, or navigation.
- Shelling out to the Git CLI for status or diff data.
- JSON, porcelain, or other structured output modes.
- Showing ignored files or adding an ignored-files section.
- Inspecting inside submodules.
- Terminal-width-aware truncation.
- Line-total aggregation in section headers.
- Custom theming beyond the agreed deterministic colors.
- GitHub issue tracking.
- Broader package distribution decisions beyond building the CLI.

## Further Notes

- The first implementation should prioritize correctness and stable output over advanced terminal UI behavior.
- The product contract is intentionally compact: `gs` should feel like a fast everyday status command, not a full Git dashboard.
- The PRD should become a parent beads epic; follow-up implementation tasks can attach to it.
